text.p: Metway Bank Ltd's new chief executive Greg Moynihan says Queensland mega-bank that combines Metway, Suncorp and the Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) will be open for business in December.
Whether it is December 1 or December 31 is only a matter of a few outstanding operational issues, he said.

"What is certain is all our calculations are on track. We still believe that if Metway shareholders choose to take the A$4.80 a share cash alternative, payment will be by the end of November," Moynihan told Reuters in a recent interview.
"It (the bank's start date) will be then either December 1 or late December but no longer than that," he said.
Shareholder meetings were being scheduled for next month to approve the merger with complete information documentation nearly finalised, he said.

Moynihan has been a major driving force behind Metway's plans to become part of Queensland's first big bancassurance operator with an asset base of A$19 billion and annual profits reaching more than A$200 million.
From 1988 to 1995, Moynihan was the bank's senior manager of strategic development and head of bank development until his latest appointment.
He said he had no doubt the Suncorp-Metway merger was the way banks would look in the future in Australia.
"We've had a look at bancassurance over the last couple of years," Moynihan said.

"We looked very carefully overseas. France, Spain and Portugal have been successful in obtaining a much greater depth of relationship with the customer and at the same time, a much higher return on equity," he said.
"Where we might get two to three products per customer, they were getting six, seven, eight and a high degree of customer loyalty."
Moynihan said Bank One and Wells Fargo in the United States were also models for the Suncorp-Metway giant.

"But our uniqueness is that we (Suncorp and Metway) have a very strong market position to start with as well as a wide range of customers -- an advantage local mortgage originators do not have," he said.
"But new products and a new name are needed for us -- wipe the slate clean and start again," Moynihan said.
The new organisation will have a much wider range of funding sources to underpin growth "and a higher rating will give us access to cheaper sources of funds," Moynihan said.
With a new board of non-executive directors headed by chairman John Lamble already announced, the hunt was now on for a new chief executive, Moynihan said.
"I hope I have a good role in the new group and be in a position to influence the group's future," Moynihan said.
"But it would be wrong for me to speculate on my position," he said.
